pairs.subject: motion
pairs.evidence: app/_landing/cosmos/engine/sceneSpec.ts:59 The overview declares seven infinite sway sheets, a drifting cloud bank, a pulsing lamp and a bob on every medallion. The surface has no visible stop control, the ambient travel is far past the budget, and the reduced-motion flag the scripted loops read is a snapshot taken at boot.

techniques.evidence: app/_landing/cosmos/engine/sceneSpec.ts:59 The sway loops (46-124 s periods, infinite alternate per cosmos.css:78) start on their own and run indefinitely. A search of app/_landing for pause/stop/aria-pressed found no visible, operable stop; only the OS preference and machine pauses (hidden tab, off-screen) suspend them. The pointer parallax is value-driven with clamped travel, so it is exempt.

app/_landing/cosmos/engine/sceneSpec.ts:28 The ambient drift travels ±4% of viewport width (about ±77 px at 1920), and the sway rotates large discs by up to about 4.9 deg, against a bound of a few pixels. About 9 ambient instances plus one bob per medallion run at once (more than fit on one hand). The medal bob (±3-4 px) and the 900 ms stagger cap are within budget.

app/_landing/cosmos/engine/camera.ts:32 cx.RM comes from perf.ts:99 matchMedia(...).matches, read once in index.ts:104, and no change listener exists. A preference turned on mid-session stops the CSS loops through the live media query, but the scripted parallax and carousel glide keep their boot-time copy. The fallbacks themselves are well designed: loops go still, transitions collapse to .15s rather than to zero, and the carousel snaps.

app/_landing/cosmos/engine/camera.ts:53 wirePause merges hidden-tab and off-screen into one root .paused class, but only CSS reads it. The scripted camera loop re-derives visibility from document.hidden itself and ignores the off-screen decider. setLook/frameReq also restart frames while paused, which contradicts the header's claim that the frame loop stops. There is no user-stop decider.

app/_landing/cosmos/engine/camera.ts:20 Frame values are written straight to element style (transform/opacity) outside React, on one shared rAF loop (life.ts Life.want/tick) that idles when no step wants a frame. The timestep is clamped per step (camera.ts:29, carousel.ts:41).

app/_landing/cosmos/engine/life.ts:14 Ambient and fire-and-forget motion runs on platform keyframes and transitions. The one owned scripted loop carries the retargetable, input-steered gestures (parallax, drag, carousel glide). No third-party animation library with a global switch is involved.

app/_landing/cosmos/engine/camera.ts:41 The camera is split into independent tracks: pointer look (approach k=.085), drag offset (decay .9, held while dragging) and wheel dolly (decays only after 800 ms idle). Each has its own curve and its own input axis.

app/_landing/cosmos/engine/scene.ts:133 A rebuild (resize or tier change) marks the planes and medallions .in before the new stack is connected (scene.ts:136), so the entrance does not replay. The boot mount is the only cause of the entrance, which works as a structural reset; the header states it (scene.ts:20-23).

app/_landing/cosmos/engine/scene.ts:98 A raster job that fails or is dropped resolves null (raster.ts run/drainMain catch), so Promise.all still settles and the plane is revealed rather than left armed. The hidden start state applies only to JS-built nodes, and the reduced-motion boot path calls showAll.

app/_landing/cosmos/engine/carousel.ts:323 Opening a template passes the card face's rect so the stage art FLIPs out of the card (one identity). Carousel cards stay mounted and only their transform changes. Caveat: the reduced form in stage.ts:109 keeps the match with a .01s tween rather than withdrawing the identity, which is outside this context.

app/_landing/cosmos/cosmos.css:4 The landing's motion is declared bespoke private choreography (taken from the contest design, not the kit), which the technique allows outside the shared vocabulary. Its taste numbers (e.g. medalLayer.ts:19 stagger 55/900) are inline rather than named constants.

pairs.registryProposal: reduced-motion-mechanics could name the split-liveness case directly: a CSS media query that stays live alongside a scripted flag sampled once yields a half-reduced surface after a mid-session toggle, and each half looks correct on its own.
